title: 10 Lectures and 42 Open Problems — Gaussian singular-value monotonicity
statement: For a $d\times d$ real Gaussian matrix $G_{\mathbb{R}}$ and complex Gaussian matrix $G_{\mathbb{C}}$, both normalized to entry variance $1/d$, define $\alpha_{\mathbb{K}}(d)=d^{-1}\mathbb{E}\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k(G_{\mathbb{K}})$. Is $\alpha_{\mathbb{R}}(d)$ monotonically increasing in $d$, and is $\alpha_{\mathbb{C}}(d)$ monotonically decreasing in $d$?

research_summary: - $\alpha_{\mathbb C}(d)$ is monotonically **decreasing** in $d$ — proven in the literature (arXiv:1606.00494). - $\alpha_{\mathbb R}(d)$ is conjectured to be monotonically **increasing** in $d$ — **still open** as far as verified.
